body: 01000 seems to be an error-on-connect, not during a connection, that would seem to conflict with the apparent raise during pyodbc cursor.execute() .

**Mike Bayer** has proposed a fix for this issue in the **master** branch:

**Add SQL Server 01000 disconnect** https://gerrit.sqlalchemy.org/c/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/+/2305

**Mike Bayer** has proposed a fix for this issue in the **rel_1_3** branch:

**Add SQL Server 01000 disconnect** https://gerrit.sqlalchemy.org/c/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/+/2306

Thank you very much for the speedy fix and the improved workaround!

I think the second issue is due to my imperfect example-code: I am using the pool_pre_ping in my real code, in the context of Flask-SQLAlchemy, web-endpoints, etc. The example would be better and clearer without it!

In any case I am very impressed by your fast and accurate response!!
...and I'm looking forward to the next release of SQLAlchemy! :-)

Sorry, I have a question regarding the `@event.listens_for(Engine, "handle_error")`-solution: If I try to use it with pool_pre_ping it catches an error on my query (when it is too late), not on the pre-ping.

Is that to be expected - am I using it wrong? Or is the problem somewhere "deeper in my stack"? (e.g. a connection being used without a ping because of Flask-SQLAlchemy or the way my flask is served...)

in fact you are absolutely correct, I forgot that the "ping" here fails to be part of that process.

so yes you need a patch for the immediate term:

```diff
diff --git a/lib/sqlalchemy/dialects/mssql/pyodbc.py b/lib/sqlalchemy/dialects/mssql/pyodbc.py
index 22e20c14c..cdaf08d08 100644
--- a/lib/sqlalchemy/dialects/mssql/pyodbc.py
+++ b/lib/sqlalchemy/dialects/mssql/pyodbc.py
@@ -52,7 +52,7 @@ name must be URL encoded which means using plus signs for spaces::
 
 Other keywords interpreted by the Pyodbc dialect to be passed to
 ``pyodbc.connect()`` in both the DSN and hostname cases include:
-``odbc_autotranslate``, ``ansi``, ``unicode_results``, ``autocommit``, 
+``odbc_autotranslate``, ``ansi``, ``unicode_results``, ``autocommit``,
 ``authentication`` (e.g., ``authentication=ActiveDirectoryIntegrated``).
 Note that in order for the dialect to recognize these keywords
 (including the ``driver`` keyword above) they must be all lowercase.
@@ -451,8 +451,9 @@ class MSDialect_pyodbc(PyODBCConnector, MSDialect):
     def is_disconnect(self, e, connection, cursor):
         if isinstance(e, self.dbapi.Error):
             code = e.args[0]
-            if code in (
+            if code in {
                 "08S01",
+                "01000",
                 "01002",
                 "08003",
                 "08007",
@@ -461,7 +462,7 @@ class MSDialect_pyodbc(PyODBCConnector, MSDialect):
                 "HYT00",
                 "HY010",
                 "10054",
-            ):
+            }:
                 return True
         return super(MSDialect_pyodbc, self).is_disconnect(
             e, connection, cursor

```


will add a separate issue for the ping thing.

issue.title: move handle_error listener from engine to dialect; implement for pre_ping handler

labels.name: near-term release
labels.description: addition to the milestone which indicates this should be in a near-term release

issue.body: as noted in #5646 there's a [recipe](https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/13/core/events.html?highlight=handle_error#sqlalchemy.events.ConnectionEvents.handle_error) to augment the is_disconnect() handler.  however we don't consult it in dialect pre-ping.  looks like we can add classlevel "_handle_dbapi_exception_noconnection" pretty easily to at least allow the hook to be consulted.

body:
oh, *or*, you could use the legacy recipe too:

https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/13/core/pooling.html#custom-legacy-pessimistic-ping

Thank you for all your work, the comments and the new workarounds!

Judging by all the complications involved in using event-hooks to add an additional `is_disconnected`-code, my original workaround (inheriting the dialect and adding it to the dialect-registry) looks comparatively painless to me. Is there any deeper reason NOT to use a fix along that line?
oh you're actually registering it, heh.   sure that should be fine.   i was hoping my documented techniques actually worked here but since we've stumbled on that, you should be fine throughout 1.3.

labels.name: external driver issues
labels.description: the issue involves a misbehavior on the part of the DBAPI itself, probably not SQLAlchemy

issue.body:
**Describe the bug**
The mssql-pyodbc dialect fails to recognize the failure of the server to resume a transaction. (It doesn't expect the error-code "42000".)

**Expected behavior**
The result of a restart should be understood as an `is_disconnect`-error, e.g. to trigger a reconnect.

**To Reproduce**
```py
from sqlalchemy import create_engine
from sqlalchemy.orm import sessionmaker

engine = create_engine(
    "mssql+pyodbc:///?odbc_connect=DRIVER%3D%7BODBC+Driver+17+for+SQL+Server%7D%3BSERVER%3D127.0.0.1%2C1433%3BDATABASE%3DXXXXXXXXX%3BUID%3DXX%3BPWD%3DXXXXXXXXX%3BAUTOTRANSLATE%3Dno",
    pool_size=30,
    max_overflow=0,
    pool_pre_ping=True,
    isolation_level="READ COMMITTED"
)
session_factory = sessionmaker(bind=engine)
session = session_factory()
session.execute('SELECT 1')  # this proves that everything was working OK
session.execute('SELECT 1')  # this yields the aforementioned error
```
